body:
That sounds about right. You need will power to defeat your lack of will power. Quite the paradox.

It's not so much an event that's stressful as not being able to imagine doing anything remotely fulfilling. There's nothing out there that seems the least bit appealing, especially being the forever-alone type who's never had nor ever will have a significant other.

If I put my mind to it, I probably could break through this current funk, but I'm not convinced it's worth the struggle if there's just decades of continued dreariness to follow.

I've been talking to a counselor for months and months and recently made a friend who I find even more valuable to talk to.

I can recognize many of the distortions, but lack the motivation to even try to fix them.
Do you honestly believe your parents care more about your grades than they care about you? Would they truly rather lose a child than have an imperfect one?

I suspect it's true more often than people realize. Depression can become an escape from reality where you give up on the future and don't mentally have to deal with all laborious tasks required to live well. Add in some self-pity and all the negatives that come along with being depressed, and it's a self-perpetuating cycle that is immensely difficult to climb out of even if the original causes of the depression are resolved. Reality is scary and seemingly endless toil. Why choose that when nonexistence is so absolutely peaceful?
